sources.note: No statement about Manabo/Muyadan stress or tone. About fifteen McFarland Manabo forms are cited in Zorc's accent orthography, most with a final-syllable acute (e.g. (051) 'Manabo ʔayat|ón', (054) 'Manabo kayyán', (055) 'Manabo, Luba, Itg layús', (056) 'Manabo, Itg, Blw sabáli' [penult], (160) 'Manabo basát', (167) 'Ilk, Manabo, Sbl pasaplák'), i.e. data with lexical penult/final accent marking only; the only stress remarks in the paper concern other languages (Tagalog tágtag n., *kətún). sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 2020. 'MANABO. Manabo, Abra. Abbreviation: MAN' -- working file Manabo=McFarland.rtf (dated 2020-11-25) in Zorc's McFarland Northern-Philippine data folder: 60 Manabo items from McFarland 1977 re-keyed in Zorc's accent orthography with PPH/PAN etymologies and sound-change notes. Unpublished web file.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No rule stated; every keyed form carries one acute accent, converting McFarland's penult length into penult accent and unmarked forms into final accent: of 60 items, 25 penult-accented (ʔábuŋ 'house', ʔáŋos 'breathe', báyu 'pound rice', dágum 'needle', kídoy 'eyebrow', ʔútok 'brain') and 25 final-accented (ʔapúy 'fire', ʔasín 'salt', ʔatá 'eye', bagí 'body', danúm 'water', kukú 'fingernail'), 10 unmarked/phrasal; notes such as 'loss of vowel length' (kułáp < *kúlap; mugíŋ < *múRiŋ; ʔuɫú < *qúluh) and 'gemination' (ʔuttut). Evidence of a lexical penult/final accent contrast in Muyadan as data,…

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2016. Ethnologue 19th ed., 'Itneg, Moyadan' [ity] (the Internet Archive 2017)
sources.note: 12,000 (2003 SIL), Abra; dialects 'None known'; lexical similarity 85% Masadiit Sallapadan, 76% Binongan, 75% Inlaod, 73% Maeng, 68% Ilocano. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Abaya, Digna Jocelyn, Marciana De Vera & Manuel Bajet. 2011. Dialects, beliefs and practices of the Tinguians of Abra. JPAIR Multidisciplinary Research 6(1): 77-89. doi:10.7719/jpair.v6i1.137.
sources.note: No phonology content: the 'dialects' part is a table of dialect names by municipality/barangay and a table of tribal origins; the only linguistic remark is second-hand (p.81): 'as stated in the study of Begnalen (2009), despite differences in points of origin, the phonemic similarity could be traced with slight variation across dialects'; the rest is marriage/death/burial ethnography. No word data, nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Himes, Ronald S. 1997. Reconstructions in Kalinga-Itneg. Oceanic Linguistics 36(1): 102-134. doi:10.2307/3623072
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction. Sec. 2.1 (p.106): PKI vowels '*i *i *u *V: (length)'; 2.2-2.3 (pp.107-109) Itneg/Kalinga phonology are segmental only. Appendix p.130-131: Manabo (MAN) data from McFarland 1977, grouped under Masadiit Kalinga; note 2 p.132: 'In Manabo the dialect is called Muyadan rather than Masadiit.' MAN forms carry vowel-length marks (?atu:pak 'short', na?a:was 'tall', wa:kas 'day', su:lad 'cook') vs unmarked kaysan, kiyup, sabbak, lubba. No statement of stress placement.

sources.citation: Philippine Journal of Linguistics 21(2), December 1990 (whole issue, incl. Himes, An algorithm for the phonological derivation of Isinai from Proto-Central Cordilleran)
sources.note: Itneg appears only in the Reid 1974 family tree (p.1). The stress statements ('Vowel length, rather than stress, is phonemic.. Long vowels are always stressed.. stress is predictably on the ultima') concern Isinai, not Itneg. Nothing on Moyadan.

sources.citation: McFarland, Curtis D. 1977. Northern Philippine linguistic geography. Monograph Series No. 9. Tokyo: Institute for the Study of Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa (ILCAA).
sources.note: Comparative wordlist survey of northern Luzon; Himes 1997 (Appendix, p.130) took his Manabo (Muyadan) data from it, so it presumably carries McFarland's accent/length transcription for Manabo plus front-matter transcription conventions.

sources.note: Nearest modern grammar of an Itneg variety, abstract reports 'phonemic stress'; Inlaod [iti] is a different variety (Ethnologue: 75% lexical similarity with Moyadan) but Himes 1997 places Inlaod in parts of Manabo, so its stress section is the closest description available and would be the model for what Moyadan probably does.
